record.original_question:
Let ψ ∈ L2(R) be an orthonormal wavelet, and let ψ̂ denote its Fourier transform. Define the wavelet dimension function Dψ: R→N∪{0} by Dψ(ξ) := ∑_{j=1}^{∞} ∑_{k∈Z} |ψ̂(2^j(ξ+k))|^2.

Fix any function D:R→N∪{0} satisfying (D1) D is measurable and 1-periodic, (D2) D(ξ)+D(ξ+1/2)=D(2ξ)+1 a.e., (D3) ∑_{k∈Z} 1_Δ(ξ+k) ≥ D(ξ) a.e. where Δ = { ξ ∈ R : D(2^{−j} ξ) ≥ 1 for j ∈ N ∪ {0} }, and (D4) lim inf_{j→∞} D(2^{−j} ξ) ≥ 1 a.e.

Is the set { ψ ∈ L2(R) : ψ is an orthonormal wavelet and Dψ = D } path connected in L2(R) norm?

Conjecture 2.1. Let D be any wavelet dimension function, i.e., D satisfies (D1)–(D4).

artifact.status_search_result: The question is a long-standing connectivity conjecture for orthonormal wavelets with a prescribed dimension function. While certain special cases (e.g., MSF/s-elementary wavelets and tight-frame-wavelet connectivity results) have been established, the full conjecture for all orthonormal wavelets sharing a given dimension function does not appear to have been resolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Tight Frame Wavelets, their Dimension Functions, MRA Tight Frame Wavelets and Connectivity Properties
status_evidence.snippet: Studies dimension functions and connectivity in the tight frame wavelet setting; full connectivity for orthonormal wavelets with given dimension function remains conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: Connectivity questions about wavelets with prescribed dimension functions remain open in general.
